meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Dad!

examples.text: Привет! Между прочим, за бой посуды штраф.
examples.trans: Hi! By the way, there is a fine for breaking dishes.
Hi! How are things?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dad' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: No, Dad, I cannot.
My dad has old-fashioned views.
Dad has old-fashioned views!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Right, go on and clean up.

examples.text: Плохо. А вы подавали такие надежды.
examples.trans: Too bad. And you showed such promise.
Let me hug you. I am at work.

meanings.en: to hug, to put one's arms around
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will hug', paired with 'обнимать'.

examples.text: Юля, ну иди сюда, не обижайся! Иди обниму!
examples.trans: Yulia, come here, don't be upset! Come let me hug you!
The father hugged his daughter tightly.
Grisha, hug Auntie Ilona!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am Max Lavrov.

examples.text: Раньше работал поваром, теперь я официант.
examples.trans: I used to work as a cook, now I am a waiter.
I will remember it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We do not need this cuisine.

examples.text: То, что я взяла тебя, ничего не значит.
examples.trans: The fact that I hired you means nothing.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Раньше работал поваром, теперь я официант.
examples.trans: I used to work as a cook, now I am a waiter.
Working as a waiter is not easy at all.

examples.text: Но я не собираюсь менять работу.
examples.trans: But I am not planning to change jobs.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You want to be fashionable, don't you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: And why do you have no moustache?

examples.text: Настя, в чём дело? Почему ты скрываешь?
examples.trans: Nastya, what is the matter? Why are you hiding it?

examples.text: Ты почему не предупредил, что придёшь?
examples.trans: Why didn't you warn me that you were coming?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Working as a waiter is not easy at all.
Gratin, please. And rabbit for me.

examples.text: А классика никогда не уходит из моды.
examples.trans: And classics never go out of fashion.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упредить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'warned', paired with 'предупреждать'.

examples.text: Ты почему не предупредил, что придёшь?
examples.trans: Why didn't you warn me that you were coming?
And they warned me very strictly!
I wanted to warn you.

examples.trans: What is this?

examples.text: То, что я взяла тебя, ничего не значит.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will come', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.
I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

examples.trans: We are a classic French restaurant.

meanings.en: partner, associate in business or activity
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'partner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас с партнёрами переговоры тут.
examples.trans: My partners and I have negotiations here.
I am the most reliable partner.

examples.text: У него появился новый деловой партнёр.
examples.trans: He got a new business partner.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'говоры'). Common masculine noun meaning 'negotiations' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас с партнёрами переговоры тут.
examples.trans: My partners and I have negotiations here.
We will go to negotiations.

examples.text: Да, мы поедем вместе на переговоры.
examples.trans: Yes, we will go together to negotiations.

examples.text: Максим, что тут у вас вкусного?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'кормить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will feed', paired with 'кормить'.

examples.trans: Will you feed us? Me — no.

examples.trans: No, Dad, I cannot.

examples.trans: You are gravely mistaken.

examples.trans: Maxim can serve you.

examples.trans: You are gravely mistaken.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'table' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hello! Let's go to the table.

examples.text: Хорошо, я вас за столиком жду.
examples.trans: Good, I am waiting for you at the table.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, I am learning.

examples.text: Я случайно подслушал разговор по телефону.
examples.trans: I accidentally overheard a conversation on the phone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, of course.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, what sort', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто это у нас такой щедрый?
